hero.subtitle: Transparency from the start. Here you'll find answers to the most important questions about our approach, costs, and services.

q1.q: Who is your firm right for?
q1.a: We specialize in entrepreneurs, self-employed professionals, and freelancers with complex tax matters. Our focus areas include exit tax, e-commerce, healthcare professions, real estate, and corporate structures. If you're looking for proactive consulting on equal footing – not just annual tax returns – you're in the right place.

q2.a: Yes, absolutely. Many of our clients are located throughout Germany or abroad. We use modern tools for digital collaboration: video calls, cloud accounting, secure document transmission. Personal meetings are of course also possible – at our office in Düren or at your location.

q3.a: We work with DATEV for accounting and payroll – the industry standard for professional tax consulting. For digital collaboration, we use modern cloud solutions, secure document portals, and video conferencing. Collaboration is location-independent and efficient.

q4.q: How much does the initial consultation cost?
q4.a: The first consultation (30 minutes) is free of charge. We get to know each other, you describe your situation, and we clarify how we can help you. Only then will you receive a transparent offer – with no hidden costs.

q5.q: How does the initial consultation work?
q5.a: The initial consultation is non-binding and lasts approximately 30 minutes. We get to know each other, you describe your situation and questions. We give you an initial assessment and clarify whether and how we can work together. After that, you decide at your leisure whether you want to work with us.

q6.a: You don't need any documents for the initial consultation. A brief description of your situation is sufficient (e.g., "I'm planning to relocate abroad" or "I sell internationally on Amazon"). We'll discuss all details during the conversation. For specific projects, you're welcome to bring relevant documents, but it's not required.

q7.a: Our fees are based on the German Tax Consultant Fee Regulation (StBVV) or by individual agreement. For projects (e.g., exit tax consulting, structuring), we often offer flat rates – so you know from the start what to expect. For ongoing support, we work with monthly flat rates or based on actual effort. Transparency is important to us: you'll always receive a clear offer in advance.

q8.a: Yes, we offer flat rates for many services – for example, for annual financial statements, tax returns, or consulting projects. For ongoing support, we work with monthly fixed prices. This gives you planning security. We'll discuss this individually during the initial consultation.

q9.q: Will I have a dedicated contact person?
q9.a: Yes, absolutely. You have a dedicated tax consultant as your contact person – no rotation, no anonymity. Your tax consultant knows your business, your goals, and your situation. In case of absence (vacation, illness), a colleague will represent them – but your main contact person always remains the same.

q10.q: How quickly do you respond to inquiries?
q10.a: We typically respond within 24 hours (on business days). For urgent matters (e.g., ongoing audit, deadlines), often on the same day. You can reach us by phone Mon–Fri from 08:30–13:00 & 14:30–18:00.

q11.a: Yes, that's actually our standard. We use cloud accounting (DATEV), secure document portals, and video calls. Many of our clients work exclusively digitally with us – without ever having been on-site. Of course, you can also visit us personally in Düren if you prefer.

q12.q: Do you also handle ongoing bookkeeping?
q12.a: Yes. We handle financial accounting, payroll accounting, annual financial statements, and all tax returns – completely or as supplementary consulting to your internal team, as you wish. We adapt to your requirements.

q13.q: What is exit tax and who does it affect?
q13.a: Exit taxation (§ 6 AStG) affects individuals who leave Germany while holding shares in a corporation (e.g., GmbH). Upon exit, hidden reserves are taxed – even if no sale takes place. This mainly affects entrepreneurs, shareholders, and managing directors with GmbH shares. We advise you on strategies, deferral models, and tax alternatives.

q14.q: Do you also advise on e-commerce/Amazon?
q14.a: Yes, e-commerce and online trade are one of our focus areas. We advise on VAT for international platforms (Amazon, eBay, Shopify, etc.), OSS (One-Stop-Shop), FBA, dropshipping, structuring for growth, and much more. Whether you're just starting or already selling internationally – we help you grow tax-securely.

q15.q: Do you support during tax audits?
q15.a: Yes, absolutely. We accompany you throughout the entire tax audit: preparation, execution, final meeting, and objection if necessary. Our goal is for you to be well-prepared and experience no unpleasant surprises. If you've already received an audit notice, contact us quickly.

q16.q: Do you also advise on real estate?
q16.a: Yes. We advise on real estate in private and business assets, corporate models (GmbH & Co. KG, etc.), asset transfer, speculation periods, depreciation, and much more. Real estate is tax-wise highly complex – we develop solutions that fit your situation.

q17.q: Do you also support healthcare professions (doctors, pharmacies)?
q17.a: Yes, healthcare professions are one of our focus areas. We advise doctors, dentists, pharmacies, and MVZ on founding, corporate structures, real estate structures, succession planning, and ongoing support. Healthcare professions have special tax requirements – we know them.

q18.q: How quickly can I get an appointment?
q18.a: Usually within 3–5 business days. For urgent matters (e.g., tax audit, approaching deadlines), often even sooner. Just contact us – we'll find a solution.

q19.a: As tax consultants, we may offer legal consulting as an ancillary service according to § 5 Para. 1 RDG – i.e., legal consulting directly related to tax consulting (e.g., partnership agreements in a tax context). For complex legal questions, we work together with specialized attorneys.

q20.a: Yes, gladly. We accompany you from founding to growth: choice of legal form, business registration, tax office registration, ongoing bookkeeping, tax returns. We have extensive experience especially with e-commerce start-ups, healthcare professions, or planned internationalization.

q106.q: Do you also support voluntary disclosures or preventive measures?
q106.a: Yes. We advise both preventively to avoid tax criminal law risks and supportively for existing problem constellations.

q107.q: Do you advise on restructurings and conversions?
q107.a: Yes. We accompany mergers, splits, contributions, changes of form, and holding restructurings – both from a tax and conceptual perspective. The goal is always a legally sound and economically sensible implementation.

q108.q: Do you advise on shareholder conflicts or separations?
q108.a: Yes. Particularly in shareholder disputes, exits, or restructurings, tax expertise is crucial to avoid or limit economic damage.

q109.q: Can you audit existing structures for soundness?

q111.a: Both. We accompany our clients both in good times – with structuring, expansion, and optimization – and in difficult phases such as corporate crises, liquidity bottlenecks, or insolvency situations. Particularly in crises, forward-looking and reliable tax consulting is crucial.

q112.q: Are you also active in advisory capacity during corporate crises and insolvencies?
q112.a: Yes. We advise on restructurings, reorganizations, impending insolvency, insolvency filing obligations, and in ongoing insolvency proceedings. Our focus is on liability avoidance, structure preservation, and legally sound support.

hero.subtitle: What you should know about tax audits – process, rights and strategic support

wissen.intro: A tax field audit is a significant intervention for many entrepreneurs, self-employed professionals and freelancers. What often begins as a "routine audit" can quickly lead to back taxes, interest charges or even tax criminal law risks.

what.title: What is a tax field audit?
what.text1: The tax field audit is a legally regulated examination procedure in which the tax authorities comprehensively examine the tax affairs of a taxpayer. The legal basis is in particular §§ 193 ff. Tax Code (AO) and the tax audit regulations.
what.goal: Purpose of the field audit: Uniformity of taxation in compliance with the principle of proportionality.

whatIsChecked.title: What does the tax authority actually examine?
whatIsChecked.intro: As part of a tax field audit, the tax authorities do not limit themselves to a mere comparison of figures. Rather, they conduct a comprehensive business assessment in which economic processes, organizational structures and entrepreneurial decisions are comprehensively evaluated.

article.s1_title: 1. How Is a Tax Criminal Investigation Initiated?
article.s1_p1: Tax criminal proceedings are initiated as soon as there are sufficient factual indications of a tax offence. An initial suspicion is enough – proof is not yet required at this stage.
article.s1_p2: The initiation can occur through various channels, for example:
article.s1_li5: Analysis of bank, platform or foreign data
article.s1_p3: Important: The affected person often only learns about this very late or by chance.
article.s2_title: 2. Visit by Officials – Unannounced or by Letter?
article.s2_p1: In practice, it is common for officials to:
article.s2_li3: ask questions or want to see documents.
article.s2_p2: This visit does not serve informational purposes, but regularly serves to gather evidence. Even seemingly harmless conversations can later be used as incriminating statements.
article.s2_p3: Alternatively or additionally, the affected person receives:
article.s2_li4: a letter regarding the initiation of tax criminal proceedings,
article.s2_li5: a formal instruction of rights for the accused,
article.s2_p4: From this moment at the latest, the affected person is officially subject to criminal proceedings.
article.s3_title: 3. The Most Common Mistakes in This Phase
article.s3_p1: Many suspects act out of uncertainty or the desire to "set everything right". Typical mistakes are:
article.s3_li4: mixing tax cooperation with criminal defence
article.s3_li5: attempting to spontaneously clear up misunderstandings
article.s4_p1: An investigation does not mean prejudgment. Panic almost always leads to wrong decisions.
article.s4_p2: Suspects have the right to remain silent. This right to silence is not an admission of guilt, but a fundamental right of defence. Statements without full knowledge of the case file are almost always disadvantageous.
article.s4_p3: Documents should not be surrendered voluntarily. The following must be clarified:
article.s4_p4: "Off-the-record" conversations can also be used as evidence. There are no non-binding conversations in criminal proceedings.
article.s4_p5: The earlier a structured defence begins, the greater are:
article.s4_li6: the chances of limiting or discontinuing the proceedings.
article.s5_p1: A central misconception is to treat tax criminal proceedings like ordinary tax proceedings.
article.s5_li1: Tax proceedings concern the assessment of taxes
article.s5_li2: Criminal proceedings concern personal guilt, sanctions and punishment
article.s5_p3: What can be "corrected" for tax purposes is often no longer reversible under criminal law.
article.s6_p1: The first hours and days after the initiation of criminal proceedings often shape the entire case. In this phase, the following is determined:
article.s6_li1: whether statements determine the content of the case file,
article.s6_li3: whether voluntary disclosure or correction options still exist,
article.s6_li4: whether the proceedings escalate or are contained.
article.s6_p2: Many cases become problematic not because of the offence, but because of clumsy conduct.
article.s7_title: 7. Voluntary Disclosure and Tax Correction – Opportunities and Limits
article.s7_p1: Anyone who recognises that a tax return is objectively incorrect or incomplete is obliged to make a correction. If this is omitted, criminal charges may develop from it.
article.s7_p2: An effective voluntary disclosure can lead to exemption from punishment – but only if:
article.s7_li1: incorrect information is corrected and omitted information is subsequently provided,
article.s7_li2: it is made in a timely manner,
article.s7_li3: no blocking reasons exist (e.g., discovery of the offence).
article.s7_p3: The requirements are high; formal errors can render the disclosure ineffective.
article.s7_p4: Uncoordinated or incomplete voluntary disclosures are among the most common defence errors. Especially in complex cases, strategic preparation is absolutely essential.
article.s8_p1: Estimations are generally permissible in tax criminal proceedings as well. However, the following applies:
article.s8_li1: The fulfilment of the offence elements (Section 370 AO) must be established to the judge's conviction, although the extent may be uncertain,
article.s8_li2: the specific amount of tax evasion may be estimated,
article.s8_li3: estimations must be realistic, consistent and plausible.
article.s8_p2: The Federal Court of Justice confirms the admissibility of estimations, but sets clear limits for them.
article.s9_title: 9. Our Approach: Structure Instead of Knee-Jerk Reactions
article.s9_p1: We accompany clients from the first contact with investigative authorities. Our focus is on:
article.s9_li1: immediate legal assessment of the situation,
article.s9_li3: protection against inadmissible use of evidence,
article.s9_li4: early influence on the course of proceedings.
article.s9_p2: The goal is not escalation, but control, containment and a legally sound solution.

article.intro_p1: A tax field audit represents a significant disruption for many entrepreneurs, companies, and shareholders. What often begins as a ‘routine audit’ can quickly lead to back tax payments, interest charges, or even criminal tax risks.
article.intro_p2: The tax authorities do not merely review numbers but also assess, among other things:
article.intro_li3: cash register management and business decisions.
article.intro_p3: (gross profit margin benchmarks, key performance indicators, and estimation methods are often applied that may not always be appropriate for the individual case)
article.intro_p4: We support our clients comprehensively from the audit notification through to litigation before the Federal Fiscal Court. Our focus is not on mere reaction but on early structuring, legal classification, and strategic negotiation with the tax authorities.
article.what_title: What do the tax authorities actually examine?
article.what_p1: During a tax field audit, the tax authorities do not limit themselves to a mere numerical comparison. Rather, they conduct an overall business assessment in which economic processes, organizational structures, and entrepreneurial decisions are comprehensively evaluated.
article.what_p2: In particular, the following areas are the focus:
article.card1_p1: The auditors analyze how a business actually operates. This includes, among other things:
article.card1_li3: inventory management, goods movements, and service interconnections
article.card1_li4: interfaces between accounting, cash management, and day-to-day operations
article.card1_p2: Discrepancies between documented processes and actual practice are frequently treated as risk indicators — even when they are economically explainable.
article.card2_p1: Another focus area is the economic viability of the business. The tax authorities examine:
article.card2_li4: price levels compared to industry benchmarks
article.card2_p2: Internal cost calculations are frequently compared against external benchmarks. Individual characteristics such as location, target audience, business model, or entrepreneurial strategy are not always adequately considered.
article.card3_title: Cash Register Management and Cash Transactions
article.card3_p1: Proper cash register management is of particular importance — especially in cash-intensive businesses. Even formal deficiencies (e.g., missing or incomplete records) can result in:
article.card3_li1: the entire bookkeeping being called into question,
article.card3_li3: estimations pursuant to Section 162 of the German Fiscal Code (AO).
article.card3_p2: The key principle: not every formal error automatically justifies a complete rejection of the bookkeeping — however, this distinction is frequently lost in practice.
article.card4_p1: Business decisions are also increasingly coming under scrutiny during audits. These include, for example:
article.card4_li4: deliberate low-price or premium pricing concepts
article.card4_p2: Such decisions must fundamentally be respected for tax purposes. Nevertheless, they are not infrequently assessed retroactively from a business perspective during the audit and compared against standardized benchmarks.

article.bench_p1: To evaluate the aforementioned areas, the tax authorities frequently rely on:
article.bench_p3: While these instruments serve as orientation aids, they are not binding valuation standards. In practice, however, they are frequently applied schematically — without adequate consideration of the specific operational characteristics of the individual case.
article.bench_p4: It is precisely here that conflicts regularly arise, as statistical averages:
article.bench_li4: do not reflect the individual business reality,
article.bench_li6: and can effectively restrict entrepreneurial freedom.
article.approach_title: Our Approach: Individual Case Instead of Statistics
article.approach_p1: A tax field audit must not become ‘taxation by statistics.’ We therefore consistently focus on:
article.approach_li3: and placing gross profit margin benchmarks and key indicators into the specific operational context through reasoned argumentation.
article.approach_p2: The goal is to replace the tax authorities’ blanket assumptions with comprehensible, legally substantiated individual case arguments.
article.s1_title: 1. What is a tax field audit?
article.s1_p1: The tax field audit is a statutory audit procedure through which the tax authorities comprehensively examine a taxpayer’s tax affairs. The legal basis is found in Sections 193 ff. of the German Fiscal Code (Abgabenordnung, AO) and the Tax Audit Regulation (Betriebsprüfungsordnung).
article.s1_p2: Objective of the audit: Equal taxation in compliance with the principle of proportionality.
article.s2_title: 2. Who is audited — and how often?
article.s2_p1: Tax field audits do not only affect large corporations. Those audited include, among others:
article.s2_li4: businesses with or without cash registers or cash transactions
article.s2_p2: The audit frequency depends on factors such as size categories, industry, anomalies, and risk criteria of the tax authorities.
article.s3_title: 3. The Audit Notification — Announcement of the Tax Audit
article.s3_p1: Every standard tax field audit is announced by an audit notification. This must include, among other things:
article.s3_li4: any specific audit focus areas, if applicable
article.s3_warning: Important: The audit notification is not a mere formality but the first strategic point of action. Errors or ambiguities may already be legally contestable at this stage.
article.s4_title: 4. Course of the Tax Field Audit
article.s4_h4a: 4.1 Location and Duration of the Audit
article.s4_p1: As a general rule, the audit takes place on the taxpayer’s business premises. Duration and scope are guided by what is necessary.
article.s4_p2: The taxpayer is obligated to cooperate — but not without limits.
article.s4_p3: The tax authorities increasingly rely on digital analysis tools (IDEA, key performance indicator comparisons, time series analyses).
article.s5_title: 5. Estimation of the Tax Assessment Basis (Section 162 AO)
article.s5_li1: the bookkeeping has formal or material deficiencies,
article.s5_li3: cash register management is not proper.
article.s5_p2: Important: Not every formal deficiency automatically justifies a full estimation.
article.s5_p3: Case law requires that an estimation must be:
article.s5_p4: Blanket or schematic surcharges are impermissible.
article.s6_title: 6. Gross Profit Margin Benchmarks — Limitations and Case Law
article.s6_p1: The tax authorities use industry-specific gross profit margin benchmarks as comparison values. However, these may not be applied mechanically.
article.s6_p2: Key case law principles (Federal Fiscal Court / BFH):
article.s6_li1: Benchmark rates are only auxiliary tools, not rules of evidence
article.s6_li2: Deviations must be allowed to be explained on an individual business basis
article.s6_li3: Specific features of the business (location, price level, concept, target audience) must be considered
article.s6_li4: An estimation based solely on benchmark deviations would be unlawful
article.s6_p3: Case law requires an individual case assessment, not taxation by statistics.
article.s7_p1: The audit findings are discussed in the final meeting. This is often where the following is decided:
article.s7_li1: whether additional assessments are ultimately reduced,
article.s7_li2: whether matters are resolved by mutual agreement,
article.s7_li3: whether the case proceeds to the appeals process.
article.s7_p2: An unprepared final meeting is one of the most common mistakes.
article.s8_p1: After the audit is concluded, the tax office issues amended tax assessments. Possible consequences include:
article.s8_li5: initiation of tax criminal or administrative fine proceedings (if investigations have not already commenced)
article.s9_title: 9. Objection & Lawsuit Before the Tax Court
article.s9_p1: Not every audit finding must be accepted.
article.s9_p3: Where necessary, we represent our clients both in the objection proceedings and before the courts.
article.s10_p1: If indications of a tax offense emerge during the audit, the legal situation changes fundamentally. While cooperation obligations apply in the tax audit procedure, taxpayers have the right to refuse to provide information in criminal proceedings. Early legal counsel is of well-known existential importance in this context.

article2.intro_p1: A tax field audit is initially not a criminal proceeding. It serves to verify tax-related matters within the taxation procedure. However, the nature of the audit can fundamentally change at any time.
article2.critical_p1: If, during the tax field audit, factual indications emerge that tax-relevant matters were not merely reported incorrectly but were intentionally or recklessly misrepresented, the tax authorities are obligated to reassess the matter.
article2.critical_p2: From this moment on, the focus is no longer solely on the correct tax assessment but on the suspicion of a tax crime or tax administrative offense.
article2.separation_title: The Legal Turning Point: Separation of Taxation and Criminal Proceedings
article2.separation_p1: As soon as such a suspicion arises, fundamentally different legal rules apply:
article2.separation_li1: The tax audit may no longer be continued without restriction.
article2.separation_li2: The taxpayer may no longer be compelled to cooperate.
article2.separation_li3: Statements, documents, and declarations may be used as evidence in criminal proceedings.
article2.separation_p2: The audit thus moves from an administrative law procedure to a repressive investigation. It is precisely this transition that is highly sensitive in practice — and is frequently unrecognized or underestimated by those affected.
article2.triggers_title: Typical Triggers for the Transition to Tax Criminal Proceedings
article2.triggers_p1: In our advisory practice, we repeatedly observe that the transition is not triggered by ‘major confessions’ but by seemingly incidental points, such as:
article2.triggers_li1: unexplainable deviations in benchmark rates or gross profit mark-ups
article2.triggers_li2: formal deficiencies in cash register management with material significance
article2.triggers_li3: contradictory statements by business owners or employees
article2.triggers_li6: indications from cross-referencing notifications or data reconciliations
article2.triggers_warning: Important: Not every error is a criminal offense. But every thoughtless statement can establish the initial suspicion.
article2.caution_title: From This Point On: Caution with Statements and Cooperation
article2.caution_p1: A common — and consequential — mistake is wanting to ‘cooperatively complete’ the tax audit even after the initial suspicion has arisen.
article2.caution_li1: What was still permissible or required in the taxation procedure
article2.caution_li2: can pose significant risk in tax criminal proceedings.
article2.caution_p3: This is where it is decided whether:
article2.caution_li3: a matter is resolved for tax purposes, or
article2.caution_li4: an investigation proceeding with a fine, penalty order, or indictment follows.
article2.strategy_title: Strategy Change at the Right Moment
article2.strategy_p1: As soon as indications of a criminally relevant accusation emerge, a strategy change is imperative:
article2.strategy_li1: separation of tax and criminal defense
article2.strategy_li4: structured communication with the tax authorities
article2.strategy_li5: protection against impermissible use of evidence
article2.strategy_p2: This moment is not a sign of guilt but an expression of professional precaution.
article2.advice_title: Why Early Legal Counsel Is Decisive
article2.advice_p1: The transition from the tax field audit to tax criminal proceedings does not always occur openly or transparently. Those affected frequently only realize in retrospect that they have already moved into criminally relevant territory. Our task is to recognize this turning point early, classify it legally, and protect our clients from irreversible mistakes.
